transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?

I came in because my brain just sort of stalls out. I’ll have a test report or even a simple CAD note open, and I can sit there for an hour not knowing what the next sentence or checkbox is supposed to be.
When your brain stalls out like that, do you usually feel worried or on edge?
I’m not sure. It’s more like I just get stuck than feeling particularly on edge.
Did you have this kind of trouble focusing when you were a child?
No, I don’t think so. This is more recent—now I can just sit there with something simple open and not be able to figure out what I’m supposed to write or check next.
Have you been feeling down or depressed lately?
I’m not really sure. I’ve mostly just noticed getting stuck like I described.
Have you lost interest in things you usually enjoy?

Yeah. My miniature printer has had the same half-finished figure sitting there for months. And things I usually like, like yoga or walking in the woods, just feel like another task now—not something I actually want to do.
Have you been feeling sad or down most days?
I’m not sure. I haven’t really been paying attention to whether I feel sad exactly.
Have you been feeling unusually tired or low on energy lately?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t paid much attention to my energy level specifically.
Lately, have you been having trouble making decisions, even about small things?
Yeah. My brain just kind of stalls out. I’ll have a test report or even a simple CAD note open for an hour and can’t figure out what the next sentence or checkbox should be.
Over the past couple of weeks, have you been feeling down or depressed most of the day nearly every day?
I honestly can’t say for sure. I haven’t been keeping track of whether I feel down most of the day.
Have you been having trouble sleeping lately?
I’m not sure, honestly. I haven’t really noticed whether my sleep has been different lately.
Have you had thoughts that life isn’t worth living, or thoughts of hurting yourself?

On my commute, I sometimes think it would be easier if I just didn’t arrive anywhere. And the thought of steering off the road comes up sometimes—it scares me enough that I grip the wheel and pull over.
Have you had any intention to act on those thoughts about steering off the road?
I don’t think I intend to do it. The thought comes up, but it scares me—I grip the wheel and sometimes pull over until it passes.
When those thoughts about steering off the road come up, do you want to die?
I don’t know if I want to die exactly. I just think it would be easier not to arrive anywhere. But when I picture actually steering off the road, it scares me, and I pull over.
Over the past couple of weeks, have you noticed your appetite being lower than usual?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t noticed a clear change in my appetite.
In the past two weeks, have you felt sad or empty most days?
I’m not sure. I haven’t really noticed feeling sad or empty most days.
Have other people noticed that you seem slowed down lately?
Yeah. In meetings, people have started finishing my sentences because it takes me so long to answer. Even walking from my desk to the test chamber feels like I’m moving through thick syrup.
Have these problems with getting stuck and slowed down been happening nearly every day for at least two weeks?
Yeah, pretty much every day. It’s been going on for at least a couple of weeks—the slow talking and that heavy, stuck feeling when I’m walking.
Before this current period, have you ever had another time in your life when you had a similar stretch of losing interest and feeling slowed down for at least two weeks?
I don’t think so. I can’t remember having another stretch like this before.
In the past two weeks, have you been eating less than usual?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t noticed a clear change in how much I’m eating.
Have you been neglecting basic self-care, like showering or changing clothes?

I’ve mostly stopped doing my usual routines, and I haven’t really been seeing people. At work I missed an important deadline, and now coworkers have to double-check or take over parts of reports I used to handle myself.
